The abundance ratios give the silicon abundance in each star relative to hydrogen.

**Star 1**

\[
[\text{Fe/H}]_1 =0 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{n_{\text{Fe}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_1 = \frac{n_{\text{Fe}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_{\odot}
\]

\[
[\text{Si/Fe}]_1 =0.3\;\text{dex} \;\Rightarrow\; 
\frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{Fe}}}\bigg|_1 = 
\frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{Fe}}}\bigg|_{\odot}\,10^{0.3}
\]

Thus  

\[
n_{\text{Si}}(1)=\frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{Fe}}}\bigg|_{\odot}\,10^{0.3}\,
\frac{n_{\text{Fe}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_{\odot}
= \left(\frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\right)_{\odot}\,10^{0.3}
\]

**Star 2**

\[
[\text{Mg/H}]_2 =0 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{n_{\text{Mg}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_2 = \frac{n_{\text{Mg}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_{\odot}
\]

\[
[\text{Mg/Si}]_2 =0.3\;\text{dex} \;\Rightarrow\;
\frac{n_{\text{Mg}}}{n_{\text{Si}}}\bigg|_2 = 
\frac{n_{\text{Mg}}}{n_{\text{Si}}}\bigg|_{\odot}\,10^{0.3}
\]

Hence  

\[
n_{\text{Si}}(2)=\frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{Mg}}}\bigg|_2\,
\frac{n_{\text{Mg}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_2
= \frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{Mg}}}\bigg|_{\odot}\,10^{-0.3}\,
\frac{n_{\text{Mg}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\bigg|_{\odot}
= \left(\frac{n_{\text{Si}}}{n_{\text{H}}}\right)_{\odot}\,10^{-0.3}
\]

**Ratio of silicon abundances**

\[
\frac{n_{\text{Si}}(1)}{n_{\text{Si}}(2)}=
\frac{(n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_{\odot}\,10^{0.3}}
{(n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_{\odot}\,10^{-0.3}}
=10^{0.3+0.3}=10^{0.6}\approx 3.98
\]

Thus the silicon atom count in Star 1 is about 4 times that in Star 2.

**Correct choice:** (D) ~3.9.  

Answer: D
